newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary's Horn says energy price hike legal.
newsitem.headline: Hungary's Horn says energy price hike legal.

text.p: Prime Minister Gyula Horn said on Tuesday that Hungary would probably win if an energy company brought a lawsuit over the government-decreed energy price rises.
"The state can be sued. I suppose we would win because the government hasn't broken any laws," Horn said at a monthly news conference.

Belgian utility group Tractebel said on Monday it was considering suing Hungary over the energy pricing which the company said prevents it from making a profit on its investment in Dunamenti power station.

The government announced two weeks ago retail hikes of 24.5 percent for electricity and 18.8 percent for gas but did not define the margins which would be granted to energy producers and distributors, in which Western utilities invested over $2 billion last year.
Horn added that the government has kept its promise for cost-proportional energy prices as of January 1, 1997.
"We undertook to establish cost-proportional prices in the energy sector from January 1, 1997. This has happened," he said.
Horn added that the decision was bound to have some opponents.
"There is no decision everybody likes," he said.

Companies such as Gaz de France and German electricity giant RWE, which bought into the gas distribution network, were promised an eight-per-cent return on investment from January 1997 and have expressed concern that the January hikes would be too little too late to generate such profits.
Horn also said there were other factors they had to consider when taking the decision.
"The interests of other large companies, which are not energy suppliers, but energy consumers, also have to be taken into account," Horn said.
